item.title: Bacopa Monnieri
item.description:

item.title: Choline
item.description:
What it is: Choline is an essential nutrient that serves as a precursor to acetylcholine—the primary memory and learning neurotransmitter. While your body produces some choline, dietary intake often falls short, and supplementation supports cognitive function, memory, and brain health across the lifespan.

What Is Choline?

Choline is a water-soluble nutrient classified as essential (your body cannot produce enough; dietary intake required). It serves two primary functions:

  1. Neurotransmitter precursor: Converted to acetylcholine, the neurotransmitter critical for memory, learning, and focus
  2. Structural component: Incorporated into cell membranes and myelin (nerve insulation), supporting neuronal health

While choline is found in foods (eggs, meat, fish, broccoli), many people consume insufficient amounts—particularly vegetarians/vegans and those eating processed diets low in choline sources.

item.title: Magnesium L-Threonate
item.description:
What it is: Magnesium L-Threonate is a patented form of magnesium engineered to cross the blood-brain barrier and directly support neuroplasticity, memory formation, and cognitive preservation. Unlike regular magnesium, it accumulates in brain tissue to enhance synaptic density and protect against age-related cognitive decline.

What Is Magnesium L-Threonate?

Magnesium L-Threonate (branded as Magtein) is a patented form of magnesium specifically designed to cross the blood-brain barrier and increase brain magnesium levels. Unlike regular magnesium supplements, which primarily support muscle relaxation and systemic health, this form is engineered to reach the brain directly.

item.title: Brain Function Nutrients: Supporting Cognition, Mood, and Neuroprotection
item.description:
How Brain Function Works

Your brain is the most metabolically demanding organ, consuming 20% of your body’s energy despite comprising only 2% of body weight. It operates through exquisitely coordinated biochemical processes:

Neuronal Communication: The Synapse

At the heart of cognition and mood lies the synapse—the junction between neurons where information transfers:

  1. Neurotransmitter Synthesis - Precursor molecules (amino acids, vitamins) are converted into neurotransmitters
  2. Vesicle Release - Neurotransmitters are packaged and released into the synaptic cleft
  3. Receptor Binding - Neurotransmitters bind to receptors on the receiving neuron
  4. Reuptake - Neurotransmitters are recycled back into the sending neuron or metabolized

item.title: Alpha-GPC
item.description:
What Is Alpha-GPC?

Alpha-GPC (L-alpha glycerylphosphorylcholine) is a naturally occurring phospholipid found in the brain and derived from lecithin. It’s one of the most potent choline sources available, capable of crossing the blood-brain barrier efficiently and delivering choline directly to the brain.

Unlike other choline sources, Alpha-GPC has a dual mechanism: it provides choline for acetylcholine synthesis AND acts as a phospholipid component of neuronal membranes. This makes it particularly valuable for both cognitive performance and structural brain health.

item.title: CDP-Choline
item.description:
What Is CDP-Choline?

CDP-Choline (cytidine 5’-diphosphocholine, also called citicoline) is a naturally occurring phosphodiester compound that serves as a critical intermediate in the biosynthesis of phosphatidylcholine, a major neuronal phospholipid.

Unlike Alpha-GPC which is a simple choline source, CDP-Choline operates through a dual mechanism: it provides both choline (for acetylcholine synthesis) AND cytidine (for RNA synthesis and neuronal energy metabolism). This unique dual pathway makes CDP-Choline particularly valuable for comprehensive neuroprotection and brain energy.

item.title: Curcumin
item.description:
What Is Curcumin?

Curcumin is the primary active compound in turmeric (Curcuma longa), a golden spice used for thousands of years in Ayurvedic and Traditional Chinese Medicine. It comprises only 2-8% of turmeric by weight, which is why standardized curcumin extracts are far more potent than turmeric powder alone.

Curcumin is a polyphenol—a class of plant compounds with powerful antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. It’s one of the most researched natural compounds, with over 12,000 published studies demonstrating benefits across numerous health conditions.

item.title: PQQ (Pyrroloquinoline Quinone)
item.description:
What Is PQQ?

Pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ) is a small quinone molecule that functions as a powerful redox cofactor and cellular signaling compound. First discovered in bacteria in 1979, PQQ has emerged as one of the most exciting longevity and cognitive enhancement compounds in biohacking circles.

PQQ is unique among supplements because it:

  1. Stimulates Mitochondrial Biogenesis — the creation of entirely new mitochondria
  2. Functions as a Potent Antioxidant — up to 5,000 redox cycles vs. 4 for vitamin C
  3. Activates Nerve Growth Factor (NGF) — supporting neuroplasticity and brain health
  4. Protects Neurons — from oxidative stress and excitotoxicity

PQQ is considered a novel vitamin-like compound: While not yet classified as an essential vitamin, research suggests PQQ may be conditionally essential for optimal human function.

item.title: Creatine
item.description:
What it is: Creatine is the most researched sports supplement ever created, increasing ATP energy production for muscle strength, power, and endurance. Beyond athletics, it supports cognitive function, mood stability, and mitochondrial health, making it valuable for both active individuals and those seeking longevity benefits.

What Is Creatine?

Creatine is a naturally occurring compound found in muscle cells that helps produce energy during high-intensity exercise. Your body produces about 1-2 grams daily from amino acids (glycine, arginine, methionine), and you get additional creatine from meat and fish.

item.title: Lion's Mane
item.description:
What it is: Lion’s Mane is a medicinal mushroom that stimulates nerve growth factor (NGF) production, promoting neurogenesis and actual brain cell growth. Unlike stimulant nootropics, it builds long-term cognitive resilience through neuroplasticity, making it ideal for memory, focus, and neuroprotection across aging populations.

What Is Lion’s Mane?

Lion’s Mane (Hericium erinaceus) is an edible mushroom that has been used in traditional Chinese medicine for centuries. Named for its shaggy, white appearance resembling a lion’s mane, it’s unique among mushrooms for its potent effects on brain and nerve health.

item.title: Omega-3 Fish Oil
item.description:
